title: Loading the vision tower on the first image re-runs installExpertSlots: allocates a second full set of slots, swaps out the live experts, and the vision load fails
scenario: A streamed tier (for example 25%) is loaded. The vision component is deferred to first use, which is the default for `ModelConfiguration(directory:)`. The user sends an image. `OnDemandComponent.loadModule` calls `Source.checkpoint()`, whose `prepare` closure is `model.prepareCheckpoint(checkpoint)` (ModelComponent.swift:291), so Inkling2.prepareCheckpoint runs again with only the vision tensors. `expertStreaming.manifest` is still set, so it calls `installExpertSlots` again. That builds new `Inkling2Experts` for all 24 layers and calls `cache.bind()` on each, which evaluates fresh zero slot tensors: another ~2.06 GB at 25% (1.54 GB at 19%). It replaces the live model's experts through `mlp.update`, which throws away every loaded slot, and it doubles `registerLayer` counters and slotBytes. It also writes `language_model.layers.N.mlp.experts.*` keys into the vision checkpoint, so `applyCheckpoint(..., to: visionModule)` with `verify: [.all]` throws on unused keys. Result: on the ~5.3 GB app limit, 3.42 GB + 2.06 GB + 0.64 GB of vision exceeds the limit and iOS kills the app (jetsam). If it survives, image input always fails and the expert cache is reset.
evidence: Inkling2.swift:2154-2160 runs `if let runtime = expertStreaming { ... if let manifest = runtime.manifest { try installExpertSlots(...); ... return checkpoint } }` with no check that this checkpoint is the language-model one. ModelComponent.swift:283-292 sets the deferred component source's `prepare: { [weak model] checkpoint in ... return try model.prepareCheckpoint(checkpoint) }`, and `loadModule()` then calls `applyCheckpoint(source.checkpoint(), to: module)`. installExpertSlots (around 2232) calls `try cache.bind()`, which runs `eval(array)` on new `MLXArray.zeros` slot tensors.
fix: Install the slots once, and only for the language-model checkpoint. Add `private var slotsInstalled = false`. In prepareCheckpoint, run the streaming branch only when `!slotsInstalled && weights.keys.contains { $0.hasPrefix("language_model.") }`; otherwise fall through to the normal path, which leaves vision keys untouched. Set `slotsInstalled = true` after installExpertSlots succeeds.
notes: UPHELD(high): Confirmed on origin/inkling-stream. ModelComponent.swift:283-292 (prepareComponents) gives the deferred vision source `prepare: { model.prepareCheckpoint(checkpoint) }`, and AnyOnDemandComponent.loadModule calls `applyCheckpoint(source.checkpoint(), to: module)`. Source.checkpoint() reads only the vision namespaces and then runs prepare. The default is componentLoading = .onFirstUse (Load.swift:426/493). No app code outside Vendor sets excludedComponents or componentLoading, and Inkling2.init creates onDemandVision whenever visionConfiguration exists. So the first image calls Inkling2.prepareCheckpoint again with a vision-only checkpoint. expertStreaming is still set from willLoadCheckpoint (Inkling2.swift:2264), and runtime.manifest is a `let` (Inkling2ExpertStreaming.swift:344), so line 2154-2157 calls installExpertSlots with nothing checking which checkpoint this is. That gives two outcomes. (1) If the manifest leaves any layer unstreamed, the check at 2203-2205 (`weights[...experts.gate_up_proj.weight] == nil`) throws 'layer N has no experts anywhere', because the vision checkpoint has no expert tensors. The vision load fails every time and the component stays pending. (2) If every layer is streamed, the code builds new Inkling2Experts with capacity slots and calls cache.bind() (more slot memory). It calls registerLayer again, so counters and bytes double, and it swaps the live experts through mlp.update, throwing away the loaded slots. It then injects language_model.*.mlp.experts.* keys into the vision checkpoint, and applyCheckpoint's update(verify: [.all]) on the Inkling2Vision module rejects them as unused keys. Image input fails in both cases, and in case 2 the text model's expert cache is also corrupted and extra memory is allocated. The exact size of the jetsam risk depends on the tier, but the defect is real. The proposed fix works: run the streaming branch only once, and only for checkpoints that contain language_model.* keys. The non-streaming fallthrough loop just hits `continue` for vision-only weights.

UPHELD(high): I checked this against origin/inkling-stream and the defect is real.

1. **The streaming branch has no guard.** In Inkling2.swift, `prepareCheckpoint` (line 2127) runs `if let runtime = expertStreaming { languageModel.streaming = runtime; if let manifest = runtime.manifest { try installExpertSlots(...); checkpoint.weights = weights; return checkpoint } }` at lines 2153-2160. Nothing checks which checkpoint is being prepared, and nothing stops it from running a second time.

2. **The vision load calls this method again.** Inkling2 builds `onDemandVision = OnDemandComponent(.vision)` whenever a vision config exists (line 1975) and exposes it through `onDemandComponents` (line 2285). In ModelComponent.swift:283-292, `prepareComponents` sets a deferred source whose `prepare` closure calls `model.prepareCheckpoint(checkpoint)` when `loading == .onFirstUse`. That is the default in Load.swift:426/493. VLMModelFactory.swift:504 does not override `componentLoading`, and nothing outside ios/Vendor sets `excludedComponents` or `componentLoading`. When the first image arrives, `loadModule()` runs `applyCheckpoint(source.checkpoint(), to: module)`, and `Source.checkpoint()` calls `prepare`, which runs Inkling2.prepareCheckpoint on the vision-only tensors. `expertStreaming` and its manifest are still set, so `installExpertSlots` runs a second time.

3. **The second call breaks the load either way.**
   - If the manifest leaves any layer unstreamed, the loop at about line 2203 throws "layer N has no experts anywhere", because the vision checkpoint has no expert weights.
   - If every layer is streamed, the code builds new `Inkling2Experts` objects and calls `cache.bind()` on each. Each call evaluates a new set of slot tensors, so a second full set of slots is allocated. It calls `registerLayer` again and replaces the live model's experts through `mlp.update`. This happens on a GCD background thread while the model is live. It then writes the `language_model.layers.N.mlp.experts.*` keys into the vision checkpoint's weights. `applyCheckpoint` (Load.swift:477) calls `module.update(..., verify: [.all])` on the Inkling2Vision module, so it fails on those unused keys.

   In both cases image input on a streamed tier always fails. The second case also doubles slot memory and throws away the live expert cache.

The exact memory figures (2.06 GB at the 25% tier, and the jetsam outcome) are the claim's own estimates; I did not re-measure them. The functional failure is confirmed. The proposed fix is sound: run the streaming branch only once, and only when the checkpoint contains `language_model.` keys.

title: Merge with integration conflicts in MLXBackend, and taking the branch side brings back the maxKVSize bug
scenario: Merging inkling-stream into the current origin/integration (b58fc6b) conflicts in MLXBackend.swift in two places: loadLarge, which now takes `epoch:` and wraps the load report in `isCurrent(loadEpoch)` with a token-based pendingLoadKey, and makeConversation. If the makeConversation conflict is resolved by taking the branch side, `params.maxKVSize = context` comes back and `Self.applyMemorySettings(of:to:)` is dropped. Integration removed maxKVSize on purpose: on Inkling it turns the global-attention layers into rotating caches that keep only 4 prefix tokens, so the system prompt and tool specs are silently evicted. The streamed tiers set `contextTokens = 4096`, so they would hit this after 4K tokens, and `prefill.chunking = .remainder` would also be lost (extra KV-cache checkpoint copies count against the 5.3 GB limit). Taking the branch side of loadLarge would also drop the epoch guard and the token-based pendingLoadKey handling. There is no CI, so a bad resolution would not be caught before the single iPad build.
evidence: A test merge (`git merge --no-commit origin/inkling-stream` on origin/integration in a scratch clone) gives CONFLICT in MLXBackend.swift, build.yml and ENGINEERING-LOG.md. The HEAD side has `params.temperature = current.temperature; Self.applyMemorySettings(of: current, to: &params)`. The branch side has `if let context = current.contextTokens { params.maxKVSize = context }`. Integration's ModelCatalog now documents contextTokens as 'Not a maxKVSize: rotating caches would evict the system prompt'.
fix: Resolve on integration's structure. In makeConversation, keep `Self.applyMemorySettings(of: current, to: &params)`, then add `params.temperature = StreamingDiagnostics.greedy ? 0 : current.temperature` and, after applyMemorySettings, the exactPrefill override `if current.streamed != nil, StreamingDiagnostics.exactPrefill { params.prefill.stepSize = StreamingDiagnostics.exactPrefillStep }`. Never set maxKVSize. In loadLarge(target, epoch:progress:), add the ensureDownloaded call, the `Inkling2ExpertStreaming.options` assignment and the streamed `loadContainer(from: directory)` branch. Append the streaming suffix to the report inside the `if isCurrent(loadEpoch)` block (make `report` a var), and do not add the branch's `defaults.removeObject(forKey: pendingLoadKey)`.
notes:
UPHELD(high): I confirmed the claim. In a scratch clone checked out at origin/integration (b58fc6b), `git merge --no-commit origin/inkling-stream` reports a conflict in ios/AgentConsole/Inference/MLXBackend.swift with two hunks.

Hunk 1 is the load-report section of loadLarge, around line 290:
- The HEAD side wraps the report in `if isCurrent(loadEpoch)`.
- The branch side does an unconditional `defaults.removeObject(forKey: MemoryBudget.pendingLoadKey)`. Integration already handles that key with a token (lines 253-256).
- The branch side also adds the streaming suffix to a `var report`.

Hunk 2 is in makeConversation, around line 366:
- The HEAD side has `params.temperature = current.temperature` followed by `Self.applyMemorySettings(of: current, to: &params)`.
- The branch side has the greedy temperature, `if let context = current.contextTokens { params.maxKVSize = context }`, prefillStepSize and the exactPrefill override, and no `prefill.chunking = .remainder`.

Integration's applyMemorySettings doc comment (lines 79-82) says maxKVSize is deliberately not set, because it would evict the system prompt and tool specs on Inkling. The streamed catalog entries set contextTokens = 4096 (ModelCatalog.swift lines 153 and 163).

Taking the branch side of hunk 2 would bring maxKVSize back and drop chunking = .remainder. Taking the branch side of hunk 1 would drop the epoch guard and undo the token-based pendingLoadKey handling. The claimed hazard and the suggested resolution both hold. Medium severity is reasonable, since this only goes wrong if the conflict is resolved badly.

UPHELD(high): I confirmed this with a test merge. In a scratch clone at origin/integration (b58fc6b), `git merge --no-commit origin/inkling-stream` reports CONFLICT in ios/AgentConsole/Inference/MLXBackend.swift, with two conflict hunks.

1. **loadLarge.** The HEAD side is the `if isCurrent(loadEpoch) { ... let report ... }` block, and loadLarge takes `epoch loadEpoch: Int`. The branch side has `defaults.removeObject(forKey: MemoryBudget.pendingLoadKey)`, a `var report` with the streaming suffix, and no epoch guard.
2. **makeConversation.** The HEAD side has `params.temperature = current.temperature; Self.applyMemorySettings(of: current, to: &params)`. The branch side has `if let context = current.contextTokens { params.maxKVSize = context }`, the prefillStepSize line and the exactPrefill override, but not applyMemorySettings.

On integration, applyMemorySettings (MLXBackend.swift:83-91) sets both prefill.stepSize and `prefill.chunking = .remainder` for entries with residentGB. Its comment says this avoids up to about 2 extra full KV-cache checkpoint copies. So taking the branch side drops the `.remainder` chunking and brings back maxKVSize.

Integration's ModelCatalog.swift:34 documents contextTokens as "Not a `maxKVSize`: rotating caches would evict the system prompt". Lines 153 and 163 set contextTokens = 4096 on the added entries. The vendored CacheConfiguration.swift describes maxKVSize as the legacy cap that turns caches into sliding-window ones.

The conflict and the regression carried on the branch side are both real. The claimed fix keeps integration's structure, adds the branch's streaming additions and never sets maxKVSize, which is correct. I did not separately check the exact "4 prefix tokens" figure, but the claim does not depend on it.

title: A read error during expert streaming crashes the app with fatalError instead of failing the request
scenario: Any preadv failure during generation crashes the process: for example EIO from flash, or a short read or EOF after experts.bin is replaced or truncated on disk while the model holds its fd, as when a re-download overwrites it. `ensure()` runs from `route()` inside graph construction (Inkling2Experts.outputs/decode), which cannot throw, so it calls `fatalError("Inkling expert streaming, layer ...")`. The user loses the app rather than getting a failed message. The lazy-bind path (line 680) does the same.
evidence: Inkling2ExpertStreaming.swift:722-725: `let failure = read(assigned); if let failure { fatalError("Inkling expert streaming, layer \(layer): \(failure)") }`. Line 680: `do { try bind() } catch { fatalError(...) }`. Inkling2ExpertFile.read throws `.io("end of file ...")` or `.io("preadv ... errno")`.
fix: Record the error instead of crashing. Store it in the runtime (for example `runtime.fail(error)`), leave the slot unloaded (slotOf/expertOf reverted, or zeroed), return the existing ids so graph building completes, and have Inkling2TextModel.callAsFunction or `prepare` check `runtime.takeError()` after the pass and throw it (prepare is `throws`). Alternatively, use mlx-swift's error handler so the error surfaces as an MLX error. At minimum, revert slotOf/expertOf for the failed records so a retry rereads them.
notes:
UPHELD(high): I could not refute this claim; the code on origin/inkling-stream matches it.

In Inkling2ExpertStreaming.swift, `ensure(_:)` returns `[UInt32]` and does not throw (line 678). Line 680 calls `fatalError` if `bind()` throws. Lines 722-725 run `let failure = read(assigned); if let failure { fatalError("Inkling expert streaming, layer \(layer): \(failure)") }`.

`read` gets its error from `Inkling2ExpertFile.read` (lines 301-319). That function retries EINTR and EAGAIN up to 16 times. Any other errno, or a zero-byte read, throws `.io("preadv ... errno")` or `.io("end of file ...")`. So EIO, a truncated `experts.bin`, or 16 straight EINTR/EAGAIN failures crash the process instead of failing the request.

One more detail supports the claim: `slotOf`, `expertOf` and `loaded` are changed before the read (lines 705-714). Recovering would therefore also need those changes undone.

How often this triggers is a judgment call:
- EIO on internal flash is rare.
- A file replaced by rename keeps the old inode open, so it would not trigger the bug. In-place truncation or overwriting would.

The defect itself is real: an I/O failure takes down the whole app, not just the request. Medium severity is a fair rating. The proposed fix is to record the error in the runtime, undo the slot bookkeeping, and rethrow from `prepare` or the caller that can throw. That fix is sound.

UPHELD(high): I could not refute this; it is confirmed. On origin/inkling-stream, ios/Vendor/mlx-swift-lm/Libraries/MLXVLM/Models/Inkling2ExpertStreaming.swift is a new file on that branch, so the problem is not already on integration.

What the code does:
- Line 724: if `read(assigned)` returns an error, `ensure()` calls `fatalError("Inkling expert streaming, layer \(layer): \(failure)")`.
- Line 680: the lazy path does the same, `do { try bind() } catch { fatalError(...) }`.
- `ensure(_:)` is declared non-throwing (`func ensure(_ ids: [UInt32]) -> [UInt32]`), so it has no way to pass an error back to the caller.
- The file reader (lines 300-316) retries only EINTR and EAGAIN, up to 16 times. Any other errno throws `.io("preadv at ...: errno")`, and a zero-byte read throws `.io("end of file ...")`. `read()` collects that error and returns it, and line 724 turns it into a process abort.

So any I/O failure during generation kills the app instead of failing the request. Before the abort, slotOf/expertOf and `loaded` have already been updated for the failed records, so even a non-fatal path would need to roll those back.

Severity caveats (they do not refute the claim):
- These failures should be rare in practice: EIO from flash, or truncation in place.
- If a re-download replaces experts.bin by atomic rename, the open fd still points at the old file and nothing breaks. The overwrite scenario only applies to in-place truncation or rewrite.
- Medium is defensible; low would also be reasonable.

The suggested fix (record the error on the runtime, roll back the slot assignments, and rethrow it from the throwing `prepare` or the caller) is sound.

title: Resumable download gets stuck on HTTP 416 when a .part file already holds the full size, and it never checks content
scenario: A file finishes downloading, but the app is killed or suspended before `moveItem(part -> target)`. Or the build on the worker is re-made smaller. Then `<file>.part` has >= file.size bytes. The next attempt sends `Range: bytes=<size>-`. The worker's parse_range returns 'invalid' when start >= size and answers 416. RangeDownload maps that to StoreError.http(416), so every later load of that tier fails the same way and the user cannot recover in the app. Separately, a stale .part from an older build that is shorter than the new size is resumed and appended to, producing a corrupt experts.bin. Nothing verifies the per-layer sha256 in experts.json, so the model silently gives wrong output.
evidence: StreamedModelStore.swift:97 has `let have = fileSize(part) ?? 0` with no check against file.size. Line 182: `if alreadyHave > 0 { request.setValue("bytes=\(alreadyHave)-", ...) }`. worker/models.py parse_range: `if start >= size or end < start: return "invalid"`, and jobworker `_send_file` sends 416.
fix: Before the request: `if have == file.size { move part -> target; continue }`, and `if have > file.size { removeItem(part); have = 0 }`. On a 416 response, delete the .part and retry once without Range. Optionally verify the experts.json layer sha256 (or a per-file hash from the listing) before writing .complete.json.
notes: UPHELD(high): I could not refute this; the code on origin/inkling-stream confirms it. In StreamedModelStore.swift, ensureDownloaded reads `let have = fileSize(part) ?? 0` and only clamps it for the progress counter (`counter.add(min(have, file.size))`). It never compares `have` with file.size before calling RangeDownload. RangeDownload.run then sends `Range: bytes=\(alreadyHave)-` whenever alreadyHave > 0. On the server, worker/models.py parse_range returns "invalid" when `start >= size`, and jobworker.py:427-428 answers that with send_response(416). The test at worker/test_models.py:150 asserts that parse_range("bytes=10-", 10) is "invalid". In didReceive response, any status other than 200 or 206 sets failure = StoreError.http(code, what) and cancels. The .part file is never deleted on that path, so every later attempt repeats the 416 and the user cannot recover in the app. Two realistic triggers: the app is killed between the size check and moveItem (a narrow window), or a server rebuild makes the file smaller than the .part already on the device. The second half of the claim also holds. A shorter stale .part from an older build is resumed and appended to with the new build's bytes. The final check is size only (`got == file.size`), and nothing checks a hash, so a corrupt experts.bin with the right size passes and gets the .complete.json marker. Severity is low/medium, as claimed. The suggested fix is sound: if have == size, move the .part into place; if have > size, delete it and start from 0; on a 416, delete the .part and retry once without Range; optionally verify the hash before writing the marker.

UPHELD(high): I could not refute this claim. On origin/inkling-stream, ios/AgentConsole/Inference/StreamedModelStore.swift:95-101 skips a file only when the *target* already has the listed size. For the .part file, line 97 reads `let have = fileSize(part) ?? 0` and passes it to RangeDownload without comparing it to file.size. Line 182 then sends `Range: bytes=<have>-` whenever have > 0.

On the server side, worker/models.py parse_range returns "invalid" when `start >= size`, and test_models.py:150 asserts this for `bytes=10-` on a 10-byte file. worker/jobworker.py:427-428 answers "invalid" with 416. The client's didReceive (lines 203-213) accepts only 206 or 200; anything else, including 416, becomes StoreError.http(416, name), and the .part file is never removed.

So a .part with have >= size makes every later ensureDownloaded call fail with HTTP 416. That happens if the app is killed between the full write and moveItem at line 105, or if the server build is replaced with a smaller one. The app has no way out: the only removeItem calls in ios/AgentConsole are the target removal at line 104 and DocumentStore, and SettingsView only edits the base URL. Nothing deletes or resets a streamed build.

The second part also holds. A shorter stale .part from an older build is resumed with a 206 and appended to. Only the total size is checked (line 103), and no content hash or ETag/If-Range is used, so a corrupted experts.bin can be marked .complete.json.

Severity "low" is reasonable. The kill window is narrow, and in-place rebuilds of the server build are rare. The proposed fix is sound: before the request, if have == size, move the part into place; if have > size, delete it. On a 416, delete the .part and retry once without Range. Optionally send If-Range or verify hashes.
